clue.text: 21 18 24 free to drink tea, travelling thither with duke

indicators.note: something that drinks takes liquid in, so the tea goes inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free (of something)
char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at liberty sets off for a far place after a cup of tea, taking a duke along.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to other answers: 21 is LAST, 18 PLANTAGENET and 24 KING. 'travelling' turns THITHER plus D into THE THIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III, killed at Bosworth in 1485, was the final monarch of the Plantagenet dynasty to rule England.

clue.text: Scarlett reportedly killed with revolver, having missed lead piping?

parts.note: Scarlett sounds like scarlet, a shade of red

indicators.note: missing its lead means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: shot means killed with a gun

explanation.surface: A Cluedo accusation: Miss Scarlett with the revolver, not the lead piping.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Scarlett, the revolver and the lead piping are all from the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US). 'having missed lead' drops the S from SHOT, leaving HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot food is very hot, so red-hot is a fair stand-in for the intensifier; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Old woman leaves the Mystery Cat in hollow

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer there, so her letters are taken away

parts.note: Macavity, the Mystery Cat, is a character in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A feline in hiding while an elderly lady departs.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing MA from the front of MACAVITY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is an empty space within something, which is what a hollow is.

clue.text: An award taken by Scottish river along with other things?

indicators.note: the river takes the award, so the two sit side by side with the river after

parts.note: DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military award
the Forth flows past Stirling into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A medal is carried off by a river in Scotland, together with other items.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to end a list, meaning 'and similar things' or 'et cetera'.

clue.text: Initiation in diabolism? Issue making you resign!

indicators.note: the initiation, or start, of the word is its opening letter

parts.note: to emit is to give out or issue

explanation.surface: A satanic rite produces a problem that forces someone out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Demit is a formal word for giving up an office or position, a synonym of resigning.

clue.text: Naval mine, not large, used by American force

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out of the word for the mine

parts.note: a limpet is a mine attached magnetically to a ship's hull
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A US navy deploys a smaller sea mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving energy behind motion, a force that pushes something along.

clue.text: What dulls headache that is new for boozer turning in?

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is placed inside

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: turning over means reading the words in reverse order

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

explanation.surface: Someone with a hangover asks what remedy suits a drinker coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What dulls headache' is the whole definition; 'boozer' is the pub, not the drinker, and 'turning' acts on both 'for' and it together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling drug taken for headaches.

clue.text: Specialist brought to western front

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a specialist

explanation.surface: An expert is sent out to fight on the Western Front.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the forward part of a ship's bow, its front end.

clue.text: See 1
Street location lay to impressive river's south

indicators.note: in a down answer, south means below, so this piece comes after

parts.note: some can mean remarkable, as in 'that was some party'
R is the map abbreviation for river
to set something down is to lay it

explanation.surface: Instructions for where to place something on a road beside a grand river.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in Somerset, home of the Clarks shoe firm, so the capital S hides a proper noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county of Somerset contains the town of Street, so the county is where Street is located.

clue.text: Daughter, insatiable, celebrated nude

parts.note: avid means eager or greedy, insatiable

explanation.surface: A greedy girl strips off and becomes famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo's marble statue of David in Florence is the world's best-known naked sculpture.

clue.text: Gold fish coming into silent tomb

indicators.note: one thing coming into another goes inside it

parts.note: mum means saying nothing, as in 'keep mum'
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A golden fish swims into a quiet burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand building housing a grave, a monumental burial chamber.

clue.text: Opener in practice rather too rough for cricket class?

indicators.note: rough handling knocks things out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A batsman finds net practice too harsh for a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about the sport, but the cricket is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthoptera is the biological order of insects that includes crickets, grasshoppers and locusts.

clue.text: See 20
Immeasurable praise surrounding maxim recalled

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for praise goes around the other piece

parts.note: to bless is to praise, as in 'bless the Lord'

indicators.note: called back means read in reverse

parts.note: a motto is a short saying, a maxim

explanation.surface: Someone compliments a remembered saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bottomless is so deep it cannot be measured, hence limitless.

clue.text: Public certainly not in order

parts.note: when news is out it is public
of course means certainly

explanation.surface: A public statement declares that something is definitely forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of course means out of the proper sequence or turn, so not in order.

clue.text: Tensed near Scots hooligan importing MDMA?

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so the drug goes inside

parts.note: near means stingy, as does tight
ned is Scottish slang for a young thug
MDMA is the drug ecstasy, whose street abbreviation is E

explanation.surface: A young Glasgow thug smuggling ecstasy gets nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightened means drew taut, the same as tensed when said of a muscle or rope.

clue.text: Program to convey false impression about recording dish

parts.note: an app is a computer program

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for deceiving wraps the recording

parts.note: to lie is to give a false impression
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Software that spreads misinformation about a music release.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is a baked dessert, a dish of fruit in pastry.

clue.text: Food at resort hotel served up for princely family

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: grub is informal for food
a spa is a health resort
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Meals at a spa hotel are brought to a royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB SPA H, read upward, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hapsburgs were the ruling dynasty of Austria and the Holy Roman Empire, a house of princes.

clue.text: Spy with another protecting English royal line

parts.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the second spy's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: another spy is an agent

explanation.surface: Two spies guard an English dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were a dynasty of English kings who ruled from 1154 to 1485.

clue.text: Trouble dogs American behind attack

indicators.note: to dog someone is to follow them, so this piece comes next

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Problems follow an American around.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to set upon them violently, the same as attacking them.

clue.text: Without horse, deformed on entry as he famously portrayed 1/7

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the anagram goes around the letter
something deformed has its shape changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H

explanation.surface: Lacking a horse and misshapen as he comes on stage, the actor famously played Richard III.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony Sher played a hunchbacked Richard III on crutches for the RSC in 1984; Richard's 'My kingdom for a horse' explains the horseless surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African-born British actor Antony Sher won acclaim for the title role in Shakespeare's Richard III.

clue.text: Shoes fashioned here don't wear out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the foot-shaped block a cobbler makes shoes on

explanation.walkthrough: The shoemaker's block and the verb for enduring are the same four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes footwear around a wooden form, and something that endures keeps going without being used up.

clue.text: Way single chap keeps so chipper?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
one means single

indicators.note: a chap who keeps something holds on to it, so the man's letters hold the word so between them

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: How does an unattached man stay so cheerful?
explanation.walkthrough: Chipper looks like the adjective for cheerful, but here it is one who chips away at stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason cuts and dresses stone with a chisel, so he is literally someone who chips.

clue.text: A lot died with gas all around

indicators.note: turned all the way around means read in reverse

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: Many people perished in a gas attack.
explanation.definitionFit: No end is an informal idiom for a great deal, as in 'it pleased her no end'.

clue.text: Leading man needs blood — gallons

parts.note: blood means family, kin

explanation.surface: An actor in the top role needs gallons of stage blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A king leads his realm, the foremost man in the land.

clue.text: Voyeur's characteristic seen in riotous epic re-run

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A peeping Tom's trait shows up in a rowdy repeat of a film epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurience is an unhealthy interest in sexual matters, the trait that drives a voyeur.

clue.text: Inspiration from cleaner at office

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A good idea comes from the office cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry, and a muse is a source of creative inspiration.

clue.text: In consequence good time promised

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these pieces go into the word for consequence

parts.note: an end is a result or consequence
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: As a result, a pleasant evening was guaranteed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged is betrothed, pledged to marry.

clue.text: Showcase at low volume in underworld ballad

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a lay is a narrative poem or song
p is the musical marking piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A quiet song from Hades is put on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to exhibit it publicly, which is what a showcase does.
